functions.name: core_sleep
functions.brief: Sleep until any interrupt (CPU stopped, peripherals running).

functions.name: core_stop_for
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode for a number of seconds, then wake and restore clocks. Uses RTC wakeup timer (LSI). Returns after wake with PLL + SysTick restored.

params.name: seconds
params.description: Seconds to spend in Stop mode.

functions.name: core_stop_until_on_change
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode until a GPIO edge occurs on the given pad. Configures the pad as input, enables EXTI, enters Stop, and restores clocks on wake. Returns after the edge is detected.

functions.name: core_standby_for
functions.brief: Enter Standby mode with RTC wakeup after the given seconds. Does not return — MCU resets on wake. Check core_woke_from_standby() at the top of main() to detect a Standby wake.

functions.name: core_standby_until_on_change
functions.brief: Enter Standby mode until a GPIO edge on the given pad (via WKUP pin). Does not return — MCU resets on wake. Not all pads support WKUP; returns without entering Standby if the pad has no WKUP capability. On Core.U.2: pad 8 (PA0 = WKUP1) and pad 7 (PA2 = WKUP4).

functions.name: core_stop
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode (caller manages wakeup source + clock recovery).

functions.name: core_standby
functions.brief: Enter Standby (caller manages wakeup source). Does not return.

functions.name: core_woke_from_standby
functions.brief: Returns 1 if the MCU woke from Standby.

functions.name: core_clear_standby_flag
functions.brief: Clear the Standby wake flag. Call after core_woke_from_standby() returns 1.

functions.name: core_watchdog_start_seconds
functions.brief: Start the independent watchdog with a timeout in seconds (convenience). For finer control use core_watchdog_start() from core_watchdog.h which accepts milliseconds.
